title: The secrets of 気: 気になる, 気にする, 気がする, 気に入る
summary: 気 is a flowing spirit. The particle shows who does what: 気になる (it occupies my spirit), 気にする (I make it so), 気がする (a feeling is active).

blocks.text: **気** is the flowing spirit in a person, close to breath, energy or mind. One end is the steady energy: **元気** (original vigor), **病気** (sick spirit). The other end is a particular will: **やる気** (a doing-spirit). 気を付ける literally attaches your spirit to something: pay attention.
Japanese lets a person "become" a feeling: こんな気持ちになる, or 悲しい顔になる. That is what makes "X turns into my spirit" make sense in the phrases below.

blocks.jp: 彼は急に悲しい顔になった。
blocks.en: He suddenly got a sad face.

blocks.text: The expressions are confusing until you notice that **the particles tell you who does what**.

rows: X turns into my spirit: it occupies my mind
I turn X into my spirit: I worry about it (on purpose)
a feeling is active, like a smell or a sound
X enters my spirit: I like it

blocks.text: 気になる: it occupies my mind
Picture the thing walking into your spirit by itself. **気になる** is something happening to you, and it can range from intrigued to worried.

blocks.en: I can't stop thinking about that person.

blocks.text: The thing is the carriage: it turns into my spirit.
気にする: I make it my concern
Now you do the turning. **気にする** is you doing it, so it tends to mean worried, and 気にしないで is a request to control it.

blocks.jp: 小さなことを気にしないで。

blocks.text: I am the unseen carriage, and the thing takes を.
気がする: a feeling is active
Start with smells and sounds. In いい匂いがする, a good smell is active, and the smell is the carriage. 気がする works the same way: the feeling itself acts.

blocks.en: There is a strange sound outside.
I feel like I've gotten stronger.

blocks.text: It is a hunch about a whole clause (雨が降りそうな気がする), not a feeling about one noun. And when the 気 is a will to do something, 気がある means "I am inclined to".
気に入る: it enters my spirit
The picture is that the thing enters your spirit, so you like it. Both が and を occur in real Japanese: この部屋が気に入った (the room enters me) and この部屋を気に入った (I let it in). Neither is the only right picture.

blocks.jp: この部屋が気に入った。
この部屋を気に入った。
blocks.en: I liked this room. (I let it in)

blocks.text: 気に入る is also the polite way to talk about OTHER people's likes, because it avoids saying "you like" or "I want" directly.

blocks.jp: プレゼントを気に入ってくれてうれしい。
blocks.en: I'm glad you liked the present.

items: 気: the spirit, energy or mind.
**気になる**: it occupies my mind; **気にする**: I make it my concern.
**気がする**: a feeling is active; I sense it.
**気に入る**: it enters my spirit, I like it.

questions.note: Something that happens to you: the thing is the main carriage, が.
questions.en: I keep thinking about my test score.

questions.prompt: 弟は服の色＿＿気にしている。
questions.note: 気にする is you doing it on purpose, so the worry takes を.
questions.en: My little brother worries about the color of his clothes.

questions.instruction: Which one happens TO you, without you choosing?
questions.note: 気になる: it occupies my mind by itself.
A feeling is active, like a smell or a sound: 気がする.
questions.en: I have a feeling it will rain today.

questions.instruction: Which sentence means "I like this song"?
questions.note: 気に入る: it enters my spirit, I like it.

questions.prompt: 気がする means that a feeling is active, like a smell or a sound.
questions.note: The feeling itself acts, just as 匂いがする means a smell is active.
questions.en: 気がする: I have a feeling.

questions.instruction: Tap the thing that occupies the speaker's mind
questions.note: 料理 is the thing that is 気になる.
questions.en: I keep wondering about that dish.

questions.prompt: He doesn't mind the small noise.
questions.note: 気にしない: he does not make the noise his concern.
questions.en: He doesn't mind the small noise.

questions.instruction: What does 気を付ける mean?
questions.note: Your spirit is attached to something: you watch out.

questions.prompt: お母さんは＿＿で、病院へ行った。
questions.note: 病気 is a sick spirit, so going to the hospital fits.
questions.en: Mother was sick, so she went to the hospital.

questions.instruction: Which sentence means "I'm glad you liked this candy"?
options: このお菓子を気に入ってくれてうれしい。
このお菓子を気にしてくれてうれしい。
このお菓子が気になってくれてうれしい。
このお菓子に気がしてくれてうれしい。
questions.note: 気に入る is the polite way to talk about someone else's liking.

questions.instruction: Which sentence means "I feel like I forgot something"?
options: 何か忘れた気を付ける
questions.note: Say a hunch with 気がする.
気がする reports a hunch about a whole clause (犬が来る気がする); it does not take a noun as the thing you feel about.

questions.prompt: 私は日本で働く＿＿がある。
questions.note: X気がある: I am inclined to X.
questions.en: I'm inclined to work in Japan.

questions.instruction: How do you say "Don't worry about it" to a friend?
questions.note: 気にしないで asks the friend to stop making it a concern.

questions.instruction: Tap the particle that shows what she worried about
questions.note: 気にする is on purpose, so what she worried about takes を.
questions.en: She worried about what I said.

questions.note: Xが気に入る: X enters my spirit.

questions.prompt: 雨が降りそうな気がする。
questions.note: 気がする reports a feeling that is active in me.
questions.en: I have a feeling it's going to rain.

questions.prompt: 気に入る means to worry about something.
questions.note: 気に入る means to like it; worrying is 気にする.

questions.prompt: 姉はこの町が気に入っている。
questions.note: The topic 姉 is the one whose spirit the town entered.
questions.en: My older sister likes this town.

questions.prompt: 道が悪いから、＿＿付けてください。
questions.note: 気を付ける: attach your spirit, be careful.
questions.en: The road is bad, so please be careful.

questions.prompt: 妹は急に元気な顔＿＿なった。
questions.en: My younger sister suddenly looked cheerful.
questions.note: なる with に: become a face, a feeling.
